figures.caption: Table 1: Per-cell brand-mention density on the 50-prompt corpus. Within OpenAI, the withingeneration mini → non-mini jump (gpt-5.4-mini→ gpt-5.4) lifts distinct brands per run from 7.7 to 10.6 (+38%); the cross-generation mini → gpt-5.5 jump more than doubles density (7.7 → 16.4) but mixes class and generation effects. Within Anthropic, opus surfaces slightly fewer distinct brands than sonnet at the same generation (12.4–13.0 vs. 13.5).

Table 2: Per-(cell × tier) surface rate with clustered-bootstrap 95% CIs (1,000 iterations resampling the 50-prompt corpus with replacement at the prompt level). The point estimate is the fraction of (run × tier-brand) pairs in which the brand appears in the run’s completion text under any judge. Split into two blocks for legibility: head/mid tiers (top, rates in the 0.4–5.3% range) and long-tail/regional tiers (bottom, rates roughly an order of magnitude smaller). The CIs are wider than Wilson intervals over (run × brand) cells would suggest — the right clustering unit is the prompt, not the (run × brand) observation — and they should be the reference for which between-cell differences are statistically distinguishable.
